subject: Anchored capacity structure and price corridor request
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Yates <tom@starlight.ai>, procurements@starlight.ai
Cc: ops@starlight.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Anchored capacity structure and price corridor request

Hi Tom / procurement team,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. As Starlight moves toward productionizing the multimodal assistant, we want to propose a reserved capacity structure that balances predictability for both sides while protecting Starlight from GPU-market price shocks.

High-level ask:
- Baseline commit (anchored capacity) sized to expected steady-state GPU-hours/month.
- A narrow price corridor tied to a GPU index so we can offer a discount today while limiting exposure if market prices spike.
- Short-term burst buffer (pay-as-you-go) for seasonal spikes.

I attached two items: a map of usage assumptions (starlight-MAP-v2.pdf) and an illustrative pricing model (gpu-pricing-scenarios.xlsx). Can you confirm:
1) target baseline tenor you’d be comfortable committing to (12 / 18 / 24 months)?
2) procurement timing and any internal approvals required for >12 months?
3) any constraints on having an index-linked corridor (e.g., not allowed in your procurement policy)?

If helpful, we can draft a short commercial term sheet that shows the corridor mechanics (floor/ceiling, lookback window, and corridor reprice triggers). Would you like that by Friday?

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Anchored capacity structure and price corridor request

Rafael,

Appreciate the proposal and the workbook — skimmed the scenarios. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit to structure:

- Procurement policy: we typically avoid index-linking for >24 month contracts. For 12–18 months we can be flexible but need legal sign-off.
- Approval: anything that includes a variable-price trigger (even with a ceiling) needs VP Procurement sign-off.
- Tenor: prefer 12–18 months for initial deals. Longer tenors will need an executive-level business case.

Can you provide an explicit worked example: baseline GPU-hours, effective price today, corridor floor/ceiling, and what the customer invoice looks like if index moves +20% or -15%? Also include an MRR-style view for billing.

Procurement will take a look once we have a term sheet and the worked example.

—Tom

Tom — thanks, noted. Attached is a one-pager term sheet and the scenario workbook updated with explicit worked examples per your asks. Highlights below:

Proposed commercial mechanics (summary):
- Baseline: 100,000 GPU-hours/month (anchored capacity) billed monthly at an anchored unit price of $X/hour.
- Corridor: if market GPU index > +12% vs baseline lookback then price moves up incrementally (capped at +20%); if index < -10% then we provide a rebate (down to -12%). Reprice happens monthly with a 3-month lookback smoothing.
- Tenor: 18 months recommended for initial rollout; we’re flexible to 12 months with smaller discount.
- Burst: additional GPU-hours billed at on-demand rates; reserved baseline can borrow up to 15% of unused baseline for one-off spikes.

Worked examples included in gpu-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (tabs: "Baseline v1", "+20pct shock", "-15pct rebate"). I also included an MRR-style invoice stub showing how corridor adjustments would appear.

Request: can procurement confirm by Mon 21 Sep whether they need a legal-side redline before we take the term sheet to finance? If procurement is OK, I’ll route to finance for preliminary approval of the corridor / discount bands.

Thanks — attaching files again below.

Attachment stubs: gpu-pricing-scenarios.xlsx, starlight-MAP-v2.pdf

Best,

Subject: Re: Anchored capacity structure and price corridor request — sizing notes

Hi team,

Quick technical sizing notes that affect the commercial baseline (pulled from the starlight-MAP-v2 assumptions):
- Model mix: 60% chat (short seq), 30% multimodal (images + text), 10% embeddings/batch offline. This yields a ~22% higher GPU-hour per token ratio vs pure chat.
- Utilization: with continuous batching and KV cache, expect 75–82% effective utilization on reserved infra; forecasting design-critical peaks will still require the burst buffer.
- Cost levers to reduce baseline GPU-hours: mixed precision + static quantization for smaller models (~8–12% GPU-hour reduction), increased batching for inference (improves throughput but adds 10–50ms P95 latency).

Recommendation for commercial baseline: size baseline at 85% of the conservative steady-state (so 85k GPU-hours/month) and reserve a 15k GPU-hour burst bucket. That reduces committed spend while protecting SLA headroom.

Operational impact (short):
- If Starlight accepts 85k baseline + 15k burst: expected annualized committed spend is ~X; downside protection corridor triggers will be slightly narrower (we can reduce ceiling to +15% with the lower baseline).
- If baseline locked at 100k as Rafael proposed, finance will expect a larger discount to compensate for idle capacity risk early in the program.

Happy to run a sensitivity scenario with the workbook — Rafael, if you want I can create a "85k-variant" tab and circulate by EOD Mon.

—Soojin
